dedupe_keys.name: ober grafendorf eco street okostraße decentralised rainwater management

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the eco-street (Ökostraße) built in summer 2015 in Ober-Grafendorf, a town of 4,612 people in the Mostviertel region of Lower Austria, where heavy rain on sealed surfaces caused small floods and sewer overloads while droughts raised the cost of watering green spaces. On a street section 100 m long and 11 m wide, runoff drains into planted roadside strips of layered natural substrates, protected under the name DrainGarden, instead of into sewers; each cubic metre stores up to 500 litres, and the system is designed for 100-year rainfall. Plant transpiration can lower local temperature by up to 5 degrees Celsius in heat periods. The substrate costs about 100 euros per cubic metre, planting from 2 euros per square metre, and the design avoids new sewer pipes and pumping costs. It was prepared in the Interreg Alpine Space C3-Alps regional adaptation process (2011-2014), built with the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences Vienna and Zenebio GmbH, and won an Energy Globe Award and a Climate Star in 2016. The page, published in 2017 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the municipality and Zenebio. Caveats: monitoring results were still pending, and total costs vary by site. It illustrates street-scale green and blue infrastructure for climate adaptation to flood, drought and heat hazards; related records are the Augustenborg and Gomeznarro Park stormwater case studies.
name: Ober-Grafendorf eco-street (Ökostraße) decentralised rainwater management
organisations: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences Vienna (BOKU)
outcomes: A 100 m eco-street drains 100-year rainfall into planted strips, avoiding new sewer pipes; the approach has since been applied in other municipalities including Vienna.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Municipality of Ober-Grafendorf, Lower Austria and Climate Alliance Lower Austria
resources_used: scientific monitoring of water balance and microclimate
